question: What is a Khipu?
answer: A khipu (also spelled quipu) is a collection of cords and knots used in the Andes, most famously by the Inca Empire (ca. 1400–1532 CE). Khipus are among the most recognizable surviving objects from the ancient Andes and played an important role in Inca society. Although they may appear to be simple bundles of string, khipus were much more than decorative objects. They served as tools for organizing and preserving information across one of the largest empires in the Americas.
